answer: Latency-signed interaction graph. Each agent must sign every message with a key whose clock drift is continuously measured against a shared reference; the dune of accumulated timing residuals is published per identity. Honest agents sit on a stable knoll of low variance. When two identities show correlated residual curves, the system flags them as a duplicate cluster. Each extra identity costs the attacker a full independent hardware clock and calibration run, plus forfeiture of the cluster's escrowed rewards on detection. The echo of a reused timing fingerprint is the tell.
